'''Dmitry Yevgenyevich Rybolovlev''' ({{langx|ru|Дмитрий Евгеньевич Рыболовлев}}, {{IPA|ru|ˈdmʲitrʲɪj jɪvˈɡʲenʲjɪvʲɪtɕ rɨbɐˈlovlʲɪf|IPA}}; born 22 November 1966) is a [[Russian oligarch]], [[billionaire]] businessman, and investor.

Rybolovlev became chairman of the Russian [[fertilizer]] producer [[Uralkali]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crowley |first=Michael |title=Trump and the Oligarch |url=https://www.politico.com/magazine/story/2016/07/donald-trump-2016-russian-ties-214116/ |access-date=2022-03-19 |website=POLITICO Magazine |date=28 July 2016 |language=en}}</ref> In 2010, he sold his majority share of Uralkali to three Kremlin-linked oligarchs for $6.5 billion.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2018-11-16 |title=AS Monaco: Dmitry Rybolovlev and His Influence in Monaco |language=en |work=Der Spiegel |url=https://www.spiegel.de/international/world/as-monaco-dmitry-rybolovlev-and-his-influence-in-monaco-a-1238822.html |access-date=2022-03-19 |issn=2195-1349}}</ref> As of 2021, Rybolovlev had a reported net worth of [[united States dollars|$]]6.7 billion, which ranked him 391st on [[The World's Billionaires|''Forbes''{{'}}s list of billionaires]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Dmitry Rybolovlev |language=en |work=Forbes |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/dmitry-rybolovlev/#34730b333bec |access-date=9 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=The World's Billionaires |language=en |work=Forbes |url=https://www.forbes.com/billionaires/list/#version:static_search:Dmitry%20Rybolovlev |access-date=18 October 2018}}</ref> 

In 2011, Rybolovlev became the [[majority owner]] and president of the football club [[AS Monaco|Monaco]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/sep/20/monaco-money-ambition-not-many-supporters|title=Monaco have plenty of money and ambition but not many supporters {{!}} David Conn|last=Conn|first=David|date=20 September 2013|website=The Guardian|language=en|access-date=18 October 2018}}</ref> He is one of the alleged victims of Swiss art transporter [[Yves Bouvier]] as part of [[The Bouvier Affair]].

His hobbies include sailing where his yachts named '''Skorpis''' race competitively, winning the [[ClubSwan 50 World Championship]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boatsnews.com/story/32138/clubswan-50-the-skorpios-crew-led-by-dmitri-rybolovlev-becomes-world-champion|title=ClubSwan 50, the Skorpios crew led by Dmitri Rybolovlev becomes world champion|date=17 October 2019 }}</ref> and taking line honour in the 2021 [[Fastnet Race]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sailweb.co.uk/2021/08/10/rolex-fastnet-race-skorpios-takes-line-honours-in-cherbourg/|title=Rolex Fastnet Race – Skorpios takes line honours in Cherbourg|author=James Boyd|date=2021-08-10}}</ref> sailing his [[ClubSwan 125]].

== Early life and education ==
Dmitry Rybolovlev was born in a [[Russians|Russian]] family, in [[Perm, Russia|Perm.]] His parents worked at the department at the [[Perm State Medical University|Perm State Medical University named after Academician E.A Wagner]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Новости |first=Р. И. А. |date=2018-11-07 |title=Биография Дмитрия Рыболовлева |url=https://ria.ru/20181107/1532242015.html |access-date=2022-08-18 |website=РИА Новости |language=ru}}</ref>

== Business career ==
He entered the business world in 1990 after graduating from the Perm Medical Institute.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=Dmitry Rybolovlev|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/profiles/dmitry-rybolovlev/|access-date=18 October 2018|website=Bloomberg}}</ref> He worked as a doctor before going into business.<ref name=":17">{{Cite web|date=21 June 2010|title=Время разбрасывать калий|url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/1386947|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.kommersant.ru|language=ru}}</ref> As a doctor's income was no longer enough to comfortably support a family during the final years of the Soviet Union, he began his first business project, a small medical enterprise that served the workers of local factories he set up together with his father, a professor of medicine.<ref name=":18">{{Cite web|title=Дмитрий Рыболовлев, хозяин "Уралкалия". В чем соль|url=https://www.forbes.ru/forbes/issue/2008-05/11470-v-chem-sol|access-date=18 November 2021|website=Forbes.ru|date=2 May 2008 |language=ru}}</ref><ref name=":19"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Дмитрия Рыболовлева начали разводить|url=https://www.beriki.ru/2010/07/02/dmitriya-rybolovleva-nachali-razvodit|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.beriki.ru}}</ref>

Rybolovlev earned his first million dollars by reselling products, which the factories used to pay for in services rather than cash as was then a common practice in Russia.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Спаситель мира": сенсация в криминальных тонах|url=https://day.kyiv.ua/ru/article/kultura/spasitel-mira-sensaciya-v-kriminalnyh-tonah|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211118111242/https://day.kyiv.ua/ru/article/kultura/spasitel-mira-sensaciya-v-kriminalnyh-tonah |archive-date=18 November 2021 }}</ref>

In 1992, Rybolovlev went to Moscow to take a business course and received a brokerage license from the Russian [[Ministry of Finance (Russia)|Ministry of Finance]], one of the first in Russia and the first in the Perm region, which permitted him to trade and deal with securities. Upon his return to Perm, he founded a brokerage and investment company and started buying up shares of local enterprises such as Uralkali, Silvinit, Azot, Metafrax, and Solikamskbumprom.<ref name=":17" />

===Uralkali===
In early 1994, Rybolovlev persuaded directors of these and some other enterprises to establish a bank, which he headed.<ref name=":17" />

He later decided to concentrate on two assets, Uralkali and Silvinit, given that the Russian potash industry was underdeveloped at the time due to the lack of interest from investors, unlike in the oil and gas sectors. Additionally, no one had been able to acquire controlling stakes in the industry's firms.<ref name=":18" /> From 1993 to 1995, Rybolovlev's portfolio included securities of Uralkali, Silvinit, Metafrax and Neftekhimik.<ref name=":18" /> These companies jointly developed the Verkhnekamskoye potash deposit, one of the world's largest.<ref name=":18" />

The violent nature of capital accumulation in early to mid-1990s Russia, including in the country's industrially developed regions like the Perm Krai, gave rise to violent criminals battling over control of companies and imposing "protection" fees on businesses.<ref name=":19">{{Cite news|title=Дмитрий Рыболовлев: от одержимого футболом олигарха до фигуранта дела о коррупции|url=https://www.vedomosti.ru/business/articles/2018/11/08/785962-dmitrii-ribolovlev|access-date=18 November 2021|website=Ведомости|date=9 November 2018 |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=23 March 2018|title=Gangster's paradise: how organised crime took over Russia|url=http://www.theguardian.com/news/2018/mar/23/how-organised-crime-took-over-russia-vory-super-mafia|access-date=18 November 2021|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref>

Refusing to cooperate with criminal gangs, Rybolovlev was forced to hire a bodyguard in 1993 before moving his family to safety in Switzerland in 1995. He also assigned bodyguards to all the directors of his enterprises, with only one, Evgeny Panteleimonov, director of Neftekhimik, refusing to accept.<ref name=":19" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=22 October 2021|title=Борьба валдайских мальчиков — 2|url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5048937|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.kommersant.ru|language=ru}}</ref><ref name=":18" /> Together with Rybolovlev, he had insisted on stopping the supply of the company's products through a mafia-controlled straw firm, "Trade House FD". That same year, Evgeny Panteleimonov was killed at the doorstep of his house.<ref name=":20">{{Cite web|title=Рыболовлев, Дмитрий Известный предприниматель, бывший владелец ОАО "Уралкалий"|url=https://lenta.ru/lib/14190281/|access-date=18 November 2021|website=lenta.ru}}</ref><ref name=":18" />

A local gangster, Oleg Lomakin, turned out to be the organizer of the murder and was detained in April 1996.<ref name=":18" /> He accused Rybolovlev of being behind the murder, which led to Rybolovlev being arrested and spending 11 months in pretrial detention.<ref name=":20" /><ref name=":18" /> Lomakin eventually withdrew his testimony, and, together with two accomplices, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for the murder of Panteleimonov. The judge concluded that the gangsters had killed the director of the company for breaking off relations with "Trade House FD".<ref name=":18" />

In 1997, Rybolovlev was acquitted by courts of law at three levels, including the Presidium of the [[Supreme Court of Russia|Supreme Court of the Russian Federation]]. In media reports, he stated that he was extorted in jail to sell the shares of his company in exchange for his freedom, but had refused.<ref name=":18" />

==== Growth and IPO ====
Over the next 15 years, Rybolovlev focused on developing [[Uralkali]] and eventually built it into a major global enterprise.<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 January 2013|title=Uralkali to Spend $5.8 Billion to Boost Potash Capacity 80% – Business...|url=http://www.businessweek.com/news/2011-10-25/uralkali-to-spend-5-8-billion-to-boost-potash-capacity-80-.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118160826/http://www.businessweek.com/news/2011-10-25/uralkali-to-spend-5-8-billion-to-boost-potash-capacity-80-.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 January 2013|access-date=16 July 2021|website=archive.ph}}</ref>

According to the Russian business newspaper ''[[Vedomosti]]'', by 2000 he had consolidated his controlling interest in the company and begun to reform and develop it.{{Citation needed|date=July 2018}} While in 2000 the capitalization of Uralkali was around $15 million, in eight years it reached $20 billion. While the overall market outlook for mineral fertilizers improved over this time, reforms made under Rybolovlev's leadership played an important role in transforming a Soviet-era enterprise into a worldwide industry leader. In 2000, Rybolovlev replaced the entire management of Uralkali, setting an increase in labor productivity as a key indicator, and as a result, it increased by 2.5 times in the period from 2000 to 2007.<ref name=":18" />

Following this rapid growth throughout the early 2000s, in 2002 Uralkali built the Baltic Bulk Terminal in St. Petersburg port as its own transport hub, providing the company with a high-tech universal transshipment complex for mineral fertilizers, and thereby improving logistics capabilities.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Балтийский балкерный терминал достроили|url=https://www.dp.ru/a/2002/12/17/Baltijskij_balkernij_term|access-date=18 November 2021|website=dp.ru|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2016|title=АГРОХИМИКИ СТОЯТ УСТОЙЧИВО|language=ru|pages=12–17|work=ВЕСТИ МОРСКОГО ПЕТЕРБУРГА|url=https://morproekt.ru/attachments/article/826/vesti_2016_2_web.pdf|access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref>

In 2005, Uralkali and [[Belarus]]ian potash producer Belaruskali combined their trade flows via a single trader, the Belarusian Potash Company (BPC).<ref>{{Cite news|last=|first=|date=5 March 2013|title={{as written|Belarus|sian}} Potash Co says fertiliser market recovering|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/belarus-potash-idUSL6N0BXI3620130305|access-date=16 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Уралкалий завершил сделку по покупке 50% акций экспортной компании Беларуси|url=https://www.vedomosti.ru/library/news/2005/11/11/uralkalij-zavershil-sdelku-po-pokupke-50-akcij-jexportnoj-kompanii-belarusi|access-date=16 December 2021|website=Ведомости|date=11 November 2005 |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=НАША ОБЩАЯ СОЛЬ|url=http://newchemistry.ru/letter.php?n_id=579|access-date=16 December 2021|website=newchemistry.ru}}</ref> There were plans to float Uralkali on the London Stock Exchange in 2006, but Rybolovlev canceled the listing after the order book had already been closed because he considered the company's valuation by investors to be unfairly low.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Уралкалий" отменил IPO|url=https://expert.ru/2006/10/11/uralkaliy/|access-date=18 November 2021|website=expert.ru|archive-date=22 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122044428/http://expert.ru/2006/10/11/uralkaliy/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The decision turned out to be correct in many respects, since just a few days after the cancellation of the IPO, a major accident occurred at one of Uralkali's mines.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Затопленное" IPO|url=https://wek.ru/zatoplennoe-ipo|access-date=18 November 2021|website=wek.ru|language=ru}}</ref> Uralkali's IPO finally went ahead in 2007, making it one of the most successful in the history of Russian business.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Уралкалий" привлек в ходе IPO около $1 млрд|url=https://www.rbc.ru/economics/12/10/2007/5703c9619a79470eaf767598|access-date=18 November 2021|website=РБК|date=12 October 2007 |language=ru}}</ref> For 14.38% of shares, Uralkali raised almost $1 billion, with demand for shares exceeding supply by 23 times.<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 October 2007|title=Potash empire strikes back in Uralkali IPO|url=https://www.globalcapital.com/article/28mw098cdu6v3zz32mb5s/equity/potash-empire-strikes-back-in-uralkali-ipo|access-date=18 November 2021|website=GlobalCapital|language=en}}</ref> The listing attracted major international investors due to the company's strong financial results and proved to be a pivot point for the traditionally closed-off Russian chemical industry, setting new standards for corporate governance transparency.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ряд предприятия Прикамья вошли в число лидеров в рейтинге инвестиционной открытости по версии "Секрета фирмы"|url=https://www.business-class.su/news/2008/06/07/12196|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.business-class.su|language=ru}}</ref>

In June 2010, Rybolovlev sold a 53% shareholding in Uralkali to a group of Russian investors: Kaliha Finance Limited ([[Suleyman Kerimov]], 25%), Aerellia Investments Limited ([[Alexander Nesis]], 15%) and Becounioco Holdings Limited ([[Filaret Galchev]], 13.2%).<ref>{{Cite web|last=Catherine|first=Belton|date=28 May 2010|title=Rybolovlev in talks to sell Uralkali stake|url=https://www.ft.com/content/8b484088-69b4-11df-8432-00144feab49a|access-date=16 July 2021|website=www.ft.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uralkali-idUKLDE65D05U20100614|title=Russian billionaire sells 53.2 pct Uralkali stake|author=((Reuters Editorial))|work=U.S.|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> The transaction price was not disclosed but was reported to be around $5.3 billion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2010-06-14/uralkali-climbs-in-london-as-owner-rybolovlev-offloads-controlling-stake|title=Uralkali Gains as Rybolovlev Sells Controlling Stake|date=14 June 2010|website=Bloomberg|access-date=18 October 2018}}</ref>

In December 2010, Uralkali bought a 20% stake in [[Silvinit]] for $1.4 billion from Rybolovlev.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703886904576030862387026264|title=Russian Firms Set Potash Deal|last=Kolyandr|first=Alexander|date=20 December 2010|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-12040084|title=Russian potash firms set to merge|date=20 December 2010|work=BBC News|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref> The merger was finalized in July 2011, after Rybolovlev had sold the remaining shares of Uralkali.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.mining.com/two-billionaires-cashed-in-big-time-ahead-of-uralkali-bombshell-55537/|title=Two billionaires cashed in big time ahead of Uralkali bombshell {{!}} MINING.com|date=2 August 2013|work=MINING.com|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> After he had sold his stakes in 2010, Rybolovlev left Russia to permanently relocate to Monaco.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 March 2022 |title=PORTRAIT. Dmitri Rybolovlev, le discret président russe de l'AS Monaco, éloigné de Vladimir Poutine |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/monaco/portrait-dmitri-rybolovlev-le-discret-president-russe-de-l-as-monaco-eloigne-de-vladimir-poutine-59a6130c-9a03-11ec-8851-630f3e65523a? |website=Ouest France}}</ref>

====Berezniki mine collapse====
In October 2006, a freshwater spring began flowing into one of Uralkali's mines under the city of [[Berezniki]], leading the walls and pillars supporting the ceilings of large caverns to dissolve.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kramer|first=Andrew E.|date=11 April 2012|title=A Russian City Always on the Watch Against Being Sucked Into the Earth|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/11/world/europe/russian-city-on-watch-against-being-sucked-into-the-earth.html|access-date=16 July 2021|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> There were attempts to keep the mine operable, but Rybolovlev decided to close it to avoid fatalities.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Дело Баумгертнера: как эффективный менеджер стал заложником в калийной войне|url=https://www.forbes.ru/kompanii/resursy/247712-voennoplennyi-kak-vladislav-baumgertner-stal-zalozhnikom-aleksandra-lukashen|access-date=18 November 2021|website=Forbes.ru|date=22 November 2013 |language=ru}}</ref> As a result, mining equipment worth tens of millions of dollars and unexploited reserves of potash ore remained underground, but human casualties were avoided.<ref name=":3" />

As a result of the mine's collapse, large sinkholes appeared around the mine and in the city of Berezniki, forcing some 12,000 residents to evacuate their homes.<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 September 2015|title=Giant sinkhole in Perm region of Russia growing wider and deeper|url=https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/giant-sinkhole-perm-region-russia-growing-wider-deeper-1518672|access-date=16 July 2021|website=International Business Times UK|language=en}}</ref> New sinkholes continue to appear regularly throughout the Perm region though it is not clear whether all of them are caused by mining activities.<ref>{{Cite web|date=20 May 2015|title=New Sinkhole Appears in Russia's Perm Region|url=https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2015/05/20/new-sinkhole-appears-in-russias-perm-region-a46702|access-date=16 July 2021|website=The Moscow Times|language=en}}</ref> The causes of the accident were investigated by commissions of [[Rostekhnadzor]], [[Ministry of Emergency Situations (Russia)|the Ministry of Emergencies]], and the [[Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (Russia)|Ministry of Natural Resources]]. The investigation concluded that the accident occurred for geological reasons, specifically a "previously unknown anomaly of geological structure".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Страница не найдена! {{!}} Информационный портал Вести ПБ|url=https://vestipb.ru/news_306.html%20%20https:/www.icis.com/explore/resources/news/2008/11/13/9171167/uralkali-not-responsible-for-berezniki-mine-flood/|access-date=18 November 2021|website=vestipb.ru|archive-date=18 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211118120044/https://vestipb.ru/news_306.html%20%20https:/www.icis.com/explore/resources/news/2008/11/13/9171167/uralkali-not-responsible-for-berezniki-mine-flood/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Then-head of the Ministry of Emergency Situations, [[Sergey Shoygu|Sergei Shoygu]], said "the situation that we have today has been accumulating for decades. There are mistakes, including wartime, when very active and, perhaps, not very cautious works were performed".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Последствия аварии на БКПРУ-1 в Березниках проанализирует независимая экспертиза|url=http://www.permonline.ru/index.cfm?page=1151&newc=3516|access-date=18 November 2021|website=permonline.ru}}</ref>

The neutrality of the commission's report has been challenged by some observers, who argued that the report was partly written by OAO Galurgia, a company affiliated with Uralkali.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web|last=Полухина|first=Юлия|date=17 October 2016|title=Вышли деньги из провала. Как росло состояние Дмитрия Рыболовлева на фоне крупнейшей техногенной катастрофы современной России|url=https://novayagazeta.ru/articles/2016/10/16/70202-vyshli-dengi-iz-provala|access-date=16 July 2021|website=Новая газета|language=ru}}</ref> Some Russian sources claimed that Uralkali failed to undertake all the necessary work in order to fill the holes in the mines, which may have directly caused the appearance of the sinkholes.<ref name=":16" /> Uralkali repeatedly denied the allegations, with Russian economic newspaper [[Kommersant]] reporting that the company's experts carried out the backfilling of the mines based on the technical projects and mining operations plans in the volumes necessary to ensure the safety of existing mines.<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 October 2016|title=Прокурорская закладка|url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/3108627|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.kommersant.ru|language=ru}}</ref> When Rybolovlev became a shareholder in Uralkali, the company began to actively engage in backfilling the voids inherited from the Soviet era. More than 70% of the funding was provided by Uralkali, the rest came from the federal budget.<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 September 2005|title=На "Уралкалии" решают проблемы закладки шахтных пустот (Пермская обл.)|url=https://regnum.ru/news/521396.html|url-status=live|access-date=18 November 2021|website=ИА REGNUM|language=ru|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051128062207/http://regnum.ru:80/news/521396.html |archive-date=28 November 2005 }}</ref> A report in ''The New York Times'' suggested that the situation was partially caused by the fact that Berezniki began as a Soviet labor camp, and was built directly over the mine to be within marching distance of work areas.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news|last=Kramer|first=Andrew E.|title=Russian City on Watch Against Being Sucked Into the Earth|work=The New York Times |date=11 April 2012 |language=en|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/11/world/europe/russian-city-on-watch-against-being-sucked-into-the-earth.html?mtrref=undefined&gwh=84EB165B21006D6D6E8221C08EF0AFFF&gwt=pay|access-date=19 October 2018}}</ref>

'''Alleged state asset grab'''

In October 2008, Russian Vice Premier [[Igor Sechin]] reopened the investigation, prompting speculation in international news outlets, including ''The New York Times,'' that a raider attack had been launched against Uralkali.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Levy|first=Clifford J.|date=7 December 2008|title=In Hard Times, Russia Tries to Reclaim Industries|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/12/08/world/europe/08kremlin.html|access-date=16 July 2021|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The results of this investigation turned out to be almost identical to the conclusion of the first investigation, namely that the cause of the accident was a combination of geological and technological factors.<ref>{{Cite web|date=12 May 2010|title="Государство должно поддерживать такие компании"|url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/1367075|access-date=18 November 2021|website=www.kommersant.ru|language=ru}}</ref>

Industry analysts at the time considered the re-opening of the investigation "an opportunistic move to gain a foothold in that industry or take some assets", where individuals close to the top echelons of government had sought to expand into the natural resources sector, in line with Putin's view that "Russia made a colossal error in the 1990s by allowing its enormous reserves of oil, gas and other natural resources to fall into private hands."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-11-11 |title=Investors see asset grab in Russia potash mine probe |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uralkali-idUKLB37464820081111 |access-date=2022-03-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Levy |first=Clifford J. |date=2008-12-07 |title=In Hard Times, Russia Tries to Reclaim Industries |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/12/08/world/europe/08kremlin.html |access-date=2022-03-10 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

In December 2008, Uralkali pledged to pay $218 million to the Russian government as compensation for costs incurred by the mine collapse.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uralkali/update-2-uralkali-settles-218-mln-mine-costs-shares-soar-idUSLA43875520090310|title=UPDATE 2-Uralkali settles $218 mln mine costs, shares soar|author=((Reuters Editorial))|work=U.S.|access-date=19 October 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> In February 2009, the company agreed to a payment of $71.8 million to the Perm region.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uralkali-compensation/uralkali-to-pay-72-mln-for-mine-collapse-damage-idUSLC63107920090212|title=Uralkali to pay $72 mln for mine collapse damage|author=((Reuters Editorial))|work=U.S.|access-date=19 October 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

===Investment in the Bank of Cyprus===
In September 2010, Rybolovlev bought a 9.7% stake in [[Cyprus]]'s largest bank, the [[Bank of Cyprus]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Offshore fund acquires 9.7 pct of Bank of Cyprus|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/bankofcyprus-share-idUKLDE68K1ZI20100921|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306152222/http://uk.reuters.com/article/bankofcyprus-share-idUKLDE68K1ZI20100921|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 March 2016|date=21 September 2010}}</ref> Rybolovlev's investment in Bank of Cyprus followed significant financial dealings in the country. Following the [[2012–13 Cypriot financial crisis|country's deep recession]], on 25 March 2013 the [[Eurogroup]] agreed with the government of Cyprus that the Bank of Cyprus would take over the remnants of [[Laiki Bank]]. To finance the deal and save the Bank of Cyprus from bankruptcy, it was also decided that accounts over €100,000 would suffer a [[Haircut (finance)|haircut]] on their assets of about 50%, which mostly wiped out Rybolovlev's stake and ended his involvement in the Bank with a $600 million loss.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/06/world/europe/wilbur-ross-russia-bank-of-cyprus.html|title=New Commerce Secretary Was No Friend to Russians at Cyprus Bank|work=The New York Times |date=6 March 2017 |access-date=19 October 2018|language=en|last1=Higgins |first1=Andrew }}</ref> In 2012, he acquired Cypriot citizenship upon becoming an investor in the Bank of Cyprus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/sep/17/cyprus-selling-eu-citizenship-to-super-rich-of-russia-and-ukraine|title=Cyprus 'selling' EU citizenship to super rich of Russia and Ukraine|website=The Guardian|date=17 September 2017}}</ref>

===AS Monaco===
[[Image:Stadion von Monaco Seitenansicht.jpg|thumb|The nine arches of the Stade Louis II in Fontvieille.]]
Rybolovlev relocated to Monaco in 2010 and in December 2011, a trust acting on behalf of Rybolovlev's daughter Ekaterina bought a 66% stake in the [[Monaco|Monegasque]] [[association football]] club [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]].<ref name=GuardSep13>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/sep/20/monaco-money-ambition-not-many-supporters|title=Monaco have plenty of money and ambition but not many supporters|author=David Conn|date=20 September 2013|work=The Guardian|access-date=26 June 2015|author-link=David Conn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/16322948|title=Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev takes over Monaco|date=23 December 2011|access-date=17 January 2019|language=en-GB}}</ref> The club was in a bad state at the time, playing at the bottom of the French second league and highly in debt, and Monaco Palace was looking for an investor to improve the club's prospects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lefigaro.fr/sport/2011/12/14/02001-20111214ARTFIG00632-un-milliardaire-russe-va-s-offrir-l-as-monaco.php|title=Un milliardaire russe va s'offrir l'AS Monaco|date=14 December 2011|website=FIGARO|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref> According to French media reports, Rybolovlev acquired the club for a symbolic €1, but with a commitment to invest at least €100 million ($129.4 million) into the club over the next four years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lexpress.fr/actualite/sport/football/as-monaco-rybolovlev-ce-russe-qui-monte-sur-le-rocher_1271643.html|title=AS Monaco: Dmitry Rybolovlev, un Russe à la conquête du Rocher|date=10 August 2013|work=LExpress.fr|access-date=19 October 2018|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/16322948|title=Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev takes over Monaco|date=23 December 2011|work=BBC Sport|access-date=19 October 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref>

The remaining 33% stake in the club is owned by Monaco's ruling family, the [[House of Grimaldi]], with Rybolovlev's acquisition of the stake in the club approved by [[Albert II, Prince of Monaco|Prince Albert II of Monaco]]. Rybolovlev was subsequently appointed president of the club.<ref name="GuardSep13" />

Though historically Monaco is one of France's most successful clubs, they were struggling at the time of Rybolovlev's arrival, and had been relegated to the second tier of French football, [[Ligue 2]]. Étienne Franzi, Monaco's former president, and the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]], the French football authority, both gave positive assessments of the club's progress after Rybolovlev's first year of ownership in December 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Comment Dmitry Rybolovlev a transfiguré l'AS Monaco?|url=http://www.nicematin.com/as-monaco/comment-dmitry-rybolovlev-a-transfigure-las-monaco.1095376.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121231135603/http://www.nicematin.com/as-monaco/comment-dmitry-rybolovlev-a-transfigure-las-monaco.1095376.html|archive-date=31 December 2012|access-date=28 December 2012}} Retrieved 28 December 2012.</ref>

In May 2013, Monaco was promoted to [[Ligue 1]] after securing the second-division title. Monaco became one of the most prodigious spenders in European football in the summer of 2013 under Rybolovlev's presidency, spending [[Pound sterling|£]]146 million on players including [[Radamel Falcao]], [[James Rodríguez]] and [[João Moutinho]]. [[Ricardo Carvalho]] and [[Eric Abidal]] were also signed on [[free transfer (association football)|free transfer]]s with large salaries.<ref name="GuardSep13" /><ref name="GuardSep14">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/sep/04/monaco-radamel-falcao-manchester-united-dmitry-rybolovlev|title=Falcao and the Monaco exodus: What's going on at last year's big spenders?|author=Paul Doyle|date=4 September 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref>

Rodríguez and Falcao subsequently left Monaco in the summer of 2014, the latter leaving on loan to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] (returning to Monaco in 2016<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 May 2016|title=Radamel Falcao returns to Monaco after Chelsea decline purchase option|url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/radamel-falcao-returns-to-monaco-after-chelsea-decline-purchase-option/17231154|access-date=17 January 2019|website=mid-day|language=en}}</ref>) and the former being sold to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] for almost double the transfer fee Monaco had paid [[FC Porto|Porto]] for his services one year prior.<ref name="GuardJul14">{{cite news|author=Sid Lowe|date=22 July 2014|title=James Rodríguez: will new galáctico fit into Real Madrid masterplan?|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/jul/22/james-rodriguez-real-madrid-masterplan|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> The transfers were explained by Monaco's vice president Vadim Vasilyev as part of a new strategy. He stated "There are two ways to go... One is either you invest a lot of money and do it quickly, the other is you build up an intelligent project and you have to base yourself on your academy and sound principles of working and scouting well and basically that's what we've decided to do."<ref name="GuardSep13" />

In January 2014, Monaco agreed to pay the governing body of French football, the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] (LFP), a one-off voluntary payment of €50 million to remain exempt from a ruling by the LFP that its clubs must have their head offices located in France. Based in the [[tax haven]] of [[Monaco]], the club managed to avoid the effects of tax increases in neighboring France. Rybolovlev and the head of the French league, [[Noël Le Graët]], had initially failed to find an agreement over the matter and Rybolovlev had initiated legal action against the league which was later dropped. The €50 million figure was calculated by the league as the amount saved by Monaco as a result of their unique location.<ref name="GuardSep13" /><ref name="GuardJan14">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/24/monaco-50m-france-ligue1-tax-exempt|title=Monaco pay €50m to France to stay in Ligue 1 – exempted from French tax|author=Paul Doyle|date=24 January 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> In July 2015, [[Conseil d'État (France)|The State Council]], France's highest court for administrative matters, announced that the agreement between the LFP and Monaco should be annulled, therefore AS Monaco no longer had to pay €50 million and had no obligation to move its headquarters out of the Principality.<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 July 2015|title=Monaco cash boost as tax deal is annulled|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/french-ligue-1/story/2516988/monaco-financial-boost-as-french-court-annuls-tax-deal|access-date=16 December 2021|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=9 July 2015|title=Ligue 1 : un cadeau à 50 millions pour Monaco|language=fr|work=Le Monde.fr|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/ligue-1/article/2015/07/09/ligue-1-monaco-ne-doit-plus-50-millions-a-la-lfp_4676907_1616940.html|access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref>

The departure of star players and a decline in spending was also attributed by Vasilyev to the introduction of the [[UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations]] and the resultant threat of sanctions. In an interview, Vasilyev dismissed claims that the Russian management were selling Monaco's best assets before leaving and stated that Rybolovlev remained "strongly committed" to the club.<ref name="GuardSep14" /> In a March 2015 interview with ''[[Nice Matin]]'', Rybolovlev reiterated that his plans for the club are long-term.<ref name="NiceMatinMar15">{{cite news|url=http://www.nicematin.com/monaco/foot-business-monaco-les-confidences-de-dmitri-rybolovlev.2154707.html|title=Foot, business, Monaco: les confidences de Dmitri Rybolovlev|date=27 March 2015|work=Nice Matin|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref>

In 2017, Monaco enjoyed its most successful season yet, winning the French [[Ligue 1]] title and reaching the semi-final of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Champions League]].<ref name="The Independent">{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/as-monaco-manchester-city-preview-transfer-strategy-a7630216.html|title=Monaco's policy of buying low and selling high has made them a European power at last|date=14 March 2017|work=The Independent|access-date=27 July 2017|language=en-GB}}</ref> Reflecting on the club's unexpected success, ''[[The Independent]]'' wrote that "Monaco's policy of buying low and selling high has made the club a true Champion's League power at last" and called Monaco "one of the best-run clubs in Europe".<ref name="The Independent"/> In an interview to ''Nice Matin'' in May 2018, Prince Albert II thanked Rybolovlev "for all his action in the management of the ASM".<ref>{{Cite web|last=rédaction|first=La|date=28 May 2018|title=Albert II sur la saison de l'ASM: "Je tiens à remercier M. Rybolovlev"|url=https://www.nicematin.com/football/albert-ii-sur-la-saison-de-lasm-je-tiens-a-remercier-m-rybolovlev-233807|access-date=16 December 2021|website=Nice-Matin|language=fr}}</ref>

In July 2018, media reported that Rybolovlev was a potential buyer of Chinese businessman [[Li Yonghong]]'s stake in [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]], but the deal didn't materialize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/bbc841e0-8689-11e8-96dd-fa565ec55929|title=Own goal: how AC Milan's Chinese owners lost control to a US hedge fund|date=14 July 2018|website=Financial Times|access-date=19 October 2018}}</ref>

Following an unsuccessful start to the [[2018–19 Ligue 1|2018–2019 season]], the club in October 2018 officially announced the departure of its head coach, [[Leonardo Jardim]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/leonardo-jardim-sacked-monaco-thierry-henry-frontrunner-replace-him-ligue-1-a8578841.html|title=Leonardo Jardim sacked by Monaco with Thierry Henry a frontrunner to replace him|work=The Independent|access-date=19 October 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref> On 13 October, the club confirmed [[Thierry Henry]] as the new head coach until 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bobbymcmahon/2018/10/12/the-biggest-challenge-facing-thierry-henry-as-he-gets-set-to-return-to-as-monaco/#db64e552dfc6|title=Thierry Henry Appointed The New Coach Of Monaco And Signs 3-Year Deal|last=McMahon|first=Bobby|work=Forbes|access-date=19 October 2018|language=en}}</ref> On January 25, Henry was sacked after only 20 matches, of which only five ended in victory. He was replaced by his predecessor Jardim.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Ben Church, Martin Goillandeau and George Ramsay|title=Henry sacked by AS Monaco, replaced by Jardim|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2019/01/25/football/thierry-henry-monaco-ligue-1-france-leonardo-jardim-spt-intl/index.html|access-date=10 December 2020|website=CNN|date=25 January 2019 }}</ref> In December 2019 the former Spain national team manager [[Robert Moreno]] was appointed as AS Monaco's head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Official {{!}} AS Monaco appoint Robert Moreno as their new manager {{!}} Get French Football News|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2019/official-as-monaco-appoint-robert-moreno-as-their-new-manager/|access-date=16 December 2021|website=www.getfootballnewsfrance.com|date=28 December 2019 }}</ref> In July 2020, former [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] coach [[Niko Kovač|Niko Kovac]] became Monaco's new coach, replacing [[Robert Moreno]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=20 July 2020|title=AS Monaco: Niko Kovac replaces Robert Moreno as coach|url=https://www.monaco-tribune.com/en/2020/07/as-monaco-niko-kovac-replaces-robert-moreno-as-coach/|access-date=10 December 2020|website=Monaco Tribune|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Apple Tree Partners ===
In 2012, the family trust of Dmitry Rybolovlev partnered with an American venture capitalist Seth Harrison, and his firm Apple Tree Partners (ATP), to establish a life sciences investment fund. Since its foundation, the fund has supported many US startup pharmaceutical developers working on promising drugs for serious illnesses. The Rybolovlev family trust, through its legal entities has contributed roughly 99% of the total $2.7 billion invested into the fund.<ref name=":21">{{Cite web |last=Willmer |first=Sabrina |date=3 July 2025 |title=Russian Billionaire Fights VC in Court Over Troubled Partnership |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-07-03/russian-billionaire-fights-vc-in-court-over-troubled-partnership |access-date=15 July 2025 |website=Bloomberg.com}}</ref> 

In 2025, the Rybolovlev family trust structures filed a petition in the [[Cayman Islands]], where ATP Life Science Ventures is registered, seeking the fund’s winding up and alleging mismanagement by its general partner, Seth Harrison. The petition cited concerns such as alleged excessive travel expenses charged to the fund and alleged pressure to finance investments the trust considered non-viable.<ref name=":21" /> This action followed a lawsuit initiated by Apple Tree Partners (ATP) in the Court of Chancery in [[Delaware]], in which ATP requested that the court compel the Rybolovlev trust to resume funding certain portfolio companies, warning of potential bankruptcies without additional capital. ATP said that Rybolovlev’s family trust, Rigmora, was unlawfully turning off funding for several important companies in ATP’s portfolio. In its subsequent court filings, the family trust stated that it had met all of its contractual obligations and described some of the fund’s investments as "hopeless". As of July 2025, the fund was valued at approximately $4 billion.<ref name=":21" /> The Delaware Court of Chancery issued a post-trial opinion on 5 December 2025 that orders specific performance of all but one of the capital calls and states that "there is no factual basis to question ATP’s good faith."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Willmer |first1=Sabrina |title=Russian Billionaire Must Pay Up in VC Fund Dispute, Judge Rules |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-12-06/russian-billionaire-must-pay-up-in-vc-fund-dispute-judge-rules |access-date=7 December 2025 |work=Bloomberg |date=5 December 2025}}</ref>

In April 2026, Rybolovlev scored a procedural win in the Delaware court which found that Rigmora had established sufficient grounds to proceed with its claim in the Cayman Islands seeking the liquidation of the ATP Life Science Ventures partnership and removal of the general partner from the management of the biotechnology fund.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Church |first=Steven |date=15 April 2026 |title=Russian Billionaire Wins Key Ruling Over Fund Eyed by Oaktree |url=https://news.bloomberglaw.com/business-and-practice/russian-billionaire-wins-key-ruling-over-fund-eyed-by-oaktree |access-date=22 April 2026 |website=bloomberglaw.com}}</ref>

==Controversies==

=== Pollution of Kama River ===
In June 2012, [[Green Patrol]], a Russian environmental NGO, listed Uralkali as one of the top 100 polluters in Russia, based on information gathered during the previous years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.greenpatrol.ru/ru/novosti/100-glavnyh-zagryazniteley-rossii|title=100 ГЛАВНЫХ ЗАГРЯЗНИТЕЛЕЙ РОССИИ {{!}} Зеленый патруль|website=greenpatrol.ru|access-date=9 February 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202033539/http://www.greenpatrol.ru/ru/novosti/100-glavnyh-zagryazniteley-rossii|url-status=dead}}</ref> An expedition organized into the [[Perm Krai]] by the same NGO in 2010, when Rybolovlev was still the company's owner, revealed that Uralkali's sinks contained at least 16 harmful elements (including zinc and ammonium), exceeding the maximum permissible levels by 1,850 times.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.beriki.ru/2010/04/02/rossiiskie-ekologi-obvinili-uralkalii-v-zagryaznenii-kamy|title=Российские экологи обвинили "Уралкалий" в загрязнении Камы|website=beriki.ru|language=ru|access-date=9 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121234321/http://www.beriki.ru/2010/04/02/rossiiskie-ekologi-obvinili-uralkalii-v-zagryaznenii-kamy|archive-date=21 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

According to Green Patrol's president, [[Roman Pukalov]], Uralkali failed to fully disclose a complete list of harmful elements that it routinely ejected into the local river [[Kama River|Kama]]. He described Kama water as "very polluted", declaring that small rivers around Berezniki had in fact turned into brine.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.rosbalt.ru/business/2010/04/01/724932.html|title="Зеленый патруль" добрался до Пермского края|newspaper=Росбалт|access-date=9 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121233149/http://www.rosbalt.ru/business/2010/04/01/724932.html|archive-date=21 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Furthermore, Uralkali's environmental spending under Rybolovlev was exceptionally low.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.novayagazeta.ru/articles/2016/10/16/70202-vyshli-dengi-iz-provala|title=Вышли деньги из провала|newspaper=Новая газета – Novayagazeta.ru|access-date=9 February 2017|language=ru-RU}}</ref>

=== Panama Papers scandal ===
In April 2016, it was alleged by the [[International Consortium of Investigative Journalists]] (ICIJ)<ref name="ICIJ">{{cite news|url=https://panamapapers.icij.org/20160403-divorce-offshore-intrigue.html|title=How the One Percenters Divorce: Offshore Intrigue Plays Hide and Seek with Millions|date=3 April 2016|work=ICIJ|access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> that Rybolovlev used a company registered in the [[Virgin Islands]] to hide art from his former wife Elena during their divorce proceeding.<ref name="The Art Newspaper">{{cite news|url=http://theartnewspaper.com/news/panama-papers-russian-billionaire-dmitry-rybolovlev-used-offshore-company-to-hide-art-from-wife-leak|title=Panama Papers: Dmitry Rybolovlev used offshore company to hide art from wife, leaked documents reveal|date=4 April 2016|work=The Art Newspaper|access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> Rybolovlev's use of offshore companies was described as a "textbook example of the lengths rich people go to protect their considerable wealth in case of a marital breakup" by the ''[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]]''.<ref name="SüddeutscheZeitung">{{cite news|url=http://panamapapers.sueddeutsche.de/articles/5707ea36a1bb8d3c3495b999|title=Cheating, Divorce And Panama Papers|date=8 April 2016|work=üddeutsche Zeitung|access-date=2 November 2016}}</ref> Rybolvlev and his attorneys gave statements to media reports claiming the offshore structures established by the Rybolovlev family trust pre-dated the divorce proceedings by several years (but according to [[Monseca]]'s leaked records the items at issue were moved out of Switzerland into London and Singapore which were out of his wife's reach using the Xitrans Finance Ltd owned by Family trust that only Dmitry and not his wife had access to ensuring the assets in it were not available to her in the divorce. This took place as the marriage was breaking down in 2009 just prior to the divorce according to [[Panama Papers]] reports, emails to [[Mossack Fonseca]] found in court records).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinsella |first=Eileen |date=2017-09-15 |title=Monaco's Justice Minister Resigns After Texts Reveal 'Vast Influence Peddling' in Billion-Dollar Art Fraud Case |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/monaco-justice-minister-resigns-1084301 |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=Artnet News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Liberation of Georgi Bedjamov ===
Georgi Bedjamov, President of the Federation of [[Bobsleigh]] and [[Skeleton (sport)|Skeleton]] of Russia and former co-owner of Vneshprombank, was arrested in March 2016 in [[Monaco]], after an international arrest warrant was issued against him by the Russian authorities on charges of fraudulent bankruptcy and embezzlement. Bedjamov was liberated in July 2016 by the [[Albert II, Prince of Monaco|Prince]], a decision that was later confirmed by the Monaco Appeal Court.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bedjamov : "niet" à l'extradition|url=http://www.lobservateurdemonaco.mc/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/Obs157.pdf|agency=L'Observateur de Monaco|issue=October 2016|access-date=9 November 2016|archive-date=10 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110105701/http://www.lobservateurdemonaco.mc/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/Obs157.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Russian sources alleged that Rybolovlev helped Georgi Bedjamov escape Russian authorities,<ref>{{cite news|title=Искусство инвестиций во власть|url=https://www.novayagazeta.ru/articles/2016/09/26/69959-iskusstvo-investitsiy-vo-vlast|agency=Novaya Gazeta|date=26 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Рыболовлев мутной воды|url=http://kremlnews.ru/articles.html?p2_articleid=6886|agency=The KremlNews|date=23 October 2016|access-date=9 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109223308/http://kremlnews.ru/articles.html?p2_articleid=6886|archive-date=9 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> but Rybolovlev denied these claims in an interview to the French newspaper ''[[Le Parisien]]'' in late October 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title= Nous façonnons les STARS de DEMAIN |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/sports/nous-faconnons-les-stars-de-demain-27-10-2016-6256509.php|agency=Le Parisien|date=27 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Рыболовлев заявил, что не имеет отношения к делу совладельца Внешпромбанка|url=https://www.gazeta.ru/social/news/2016/10/27/n_9266699.shtml|agency=Gazeta.ru|date=27 October 2016}}</ref>

=== Football Leaks scandal ===
In December 2016, the [[Football Leaks|Football Leaks scandal]] revealed that Rybolovlev and football agent [[Jorge Mendes]] had set up a secret system to illegally buy players' shares. Using a Cyprus-based offshore investment fund named Browsefish Limited, Rybolovlev manipulated the price of his own players through third-party ownerships (TPO).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Football-leaks-le-partenariat-obscur-entre-rybolovlev-monaco-et-jorge-mendes/762435|title=Football Leaks : le partenariat obscur entre Rybolovlev (Monaco) et Jorge Mendes|last=Rédaction|newspaper=L'Equipe.fr|access-date=13 February 2017|language=fr-FR}}</ref> Rybolovlev resorted to the use of offshore companies to hide his identity, as TPOs are illegal in Europe.<ref name="mediapart.fr">{{Cite news|url=https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/international/211216/le-trouble-business-du-proprietaire-de-las-monaco-avec-lagent-jorge-mendes|title=Le trouble business du propriétaire de l'AS Monaco avec l'agent Jorge Mendes|newspaper=Mediapart|access-date=13 February 2017|language=fr-FR}}</ref> Investigations revealed for example that football player [[Fabinho (footballer, born 1993)|Fabinho]] was already 48.5% owned by Rybolovlev when he was loaned to Monaco by [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.football365.fr/football-leaks-sombre-collaboration-entre-dmitri-rybolovlev-jorge-mendes-2860867.html|title=Football Leaks : La sombre collaboration entre Dmitri Rybolovlev et Jorge Mendes – Football 365|date=21 December 2016|newspaper=Football 365|access-date=13 February 2017|language=fr-FR}}</ref><ref name="mediapart.fr"/>

AS Monaco denied these allegations and that such a scheme was ever put into place, arguing that reports published in the French and European press to the contrary "contain false information and many inaccuracies".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/as-monaco/story/3690682/monaco-deny-trying-to-break-financial-fair-play-rules-after-football-leaks-claim|title=Monaco deny trying to break FFP rules|date=5 November 2018|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11816/11545860/monaco-deny-financial-fair-play-report-claiming-owner-dmitry-rybolovlev-tried-to-circumvent-rules|title=Monaco deny Financial Fair Play report claiming owner Dmitry Rybolovlev tried to circumvent rules|website=Sky Sports|language=en|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/football-monaco-deny-football-leaks-claims-of-offshore-set-up-to-bypass-financial|title=Football: Monaco deny Football Leaks claims of offshore set-up to bypass Financial Fair Play|date=5 November 2018|website=The Straits Times|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref>

=== Divorce ===
Elena Rybolovleva filed for divorce on 22 December 2008,<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{cite magazine|title=Divorce du siècle Dmitry et Elena Rybolovlev : comment se séparer d'un milliardaire|url=http://www.vanityfair.fr/actualites/international/articles/dmitry-et-elena-ryboloblev-comment-divorcer-dun-milliardaire/14177|access-date=2 November 2016|magazine=Vanity Fair}}</ref> citing in her divorce petition the "serial infidelity" of her husband.<ref>{{cite news|title=Trump and the Oligarch|url=https://www.politico.com/magazine/story/2016/07/donald-trump-2016-russian-ties-214116/|access-date=2 November 2016|work=Politico}}</ref><ref name="The Telegraph">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/russia/7868766/Russian-oligarch-facing-worlds-most-expensive-divorce.html|title=Russian oligarch facing world's most expensive divorce|work=The Telegraph}}</ref> On the same occasion, Elena officially asked the Geneva State prosecutor for protection of her assets from Rybolovlev.<ref name="Vanity Fair" />

In February 2014, Elena was detained in Cyprus for allegedly stealing a $28 million diamond ring she later proved her ex-husband had given her while they were still married.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://cyprus-mail.com/2014/02/24/russian-billionaires-estranged-wife-detained-in-cyprus-over-25m-ring/|title=Russian billionaire's former wife detained in Cyprus over $25m ring (updated) – Cyprus Mail|date=24 February 2014|work=Cyprus Mail|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Did This Billionaire Get Swindled Out of Millions in an Elaborate Art World Scheme?|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/vicky-ward/post_10541_b_8585654.html|work=Huffington Post}}</ref>

In May of that year, a Geneva court awarded Elena a record settlement of $4.8 billion. This would have been the most expensive divorce settlement in history at the time.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2014/05/19/russian-oligarch-faces-45-billion-swiss-divorce-settlement/9294953/|title=Russian's $4.5 billion divorce may be biggest in history|work=USA TODAY|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en}}</ref> However, Rybolovlev's lawyers successfully appealed the 2014 ruling in June 2015. The Geneva court reversed the earlier decision, ruling that Elena's settlement be reduced to 564 million [[Swiss francs]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/russian-billionaires-divorce-settlement-amount-pared-back-1434044377|title=Russian Billionaire's Divorce Settlement Amount Pared Back|last=Letzing|first=John|date=11 June 2015|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=18 October 2018|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref>

Finally, in October 2015, Rybolovlev and Elena announced they had reached an amicable settlement of their divorce, and that all legal actions in relation to the case would cease. Financial terms of the settlement were not disclosed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/france/11946463/The-most-expensive-divorce-in-history-ends-after-Russian-billionaire-reaches-deal-with-ex-wife.html|title='The most expensive divorce in history' ends after Russian billionaire reaches deal with ex-wife|date=21 October 2015 |access-date=2 March 2017}}</ref>

The court's decision acknowledged that "the possible existence of deception cannot be denied."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-28 |title=Billionaire battle rages on as Geneva court overturns dismissal of Dmitry Rybolovev's fraud case against art dealer Yves Bouvier |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2022/07/28/geneva-court-overturns-dismissal-of-dmitry-rybolovevs-fraud-case-against-art-dealer-yves-bouvier |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=The Art Newspaper - International art news and events}}</ref> Furthermore, the Geneva court returned the case to the Geneva Prosecutor's Office for further investigation into Bouvier.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-01 |title=The Never-Ending Art Fraud Battle Between Billionaires Yves Bouvier and Dmitry Rybolovlev Will, of Course, Continue |url=https://observer.com/2022/08/the-never-ending-art-fraud-battle-between-billionaires-yves-bouvier-and-dmitry-rybolovlev-will-of-course-continue/ |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Observer |language=en-US}}</ref>

In March 2023, U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman decreed that Sotheby's must confront the lawsuit filed by Rybolovlev. The suit accuses the auction house of being complicit in the former art dealer's scam, which led to overcharging Rybolovlev for 15 pieces of art.<ref name="Stempel">{{Cite news |last=Stempel |first=Jonathan |date=2023-03-01 |title=Sotheby's must face Russian billionaire oligarch's art fraud lawsuit |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/sothebys-must-face-russian-billionaire-oligarchs-art-fraud-lawsuit-2023-03-01/ |access-date=2023-05-15}}</ref> The artworks in question are worth hundreds of millions of dollars and include works by Gustav Klimt, Rene Magritte, and Amedeo Modigliani, along with ''The Salvator Mundi'', attributed to Leonardo da Vinci.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com">{{Cite web |date=2023-03-07 |title=Leonardo's Salvator Mundi heads to court in case against Sotheby's |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2023/03/07/leonardos-salvator-mundi-heads-to-court-in-case-against-sothebys |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=The Art Newspaper - International art news and events}}</ref>

The accusations in the lawsuit revolve around fraud. The judge allowed the ''Salvator Mundi'' claims and referred to evidence that Sotheby's was aware that Bouvier had purchased the painting for Rybolovlev. Sotheby's client manager collaborated with Bouvier to "adjust its valuation" despite objections from Sotheby's own Old Masters specialist.<ref name="Stempel"/> The judge's ruling also confirms that Samuel Valette, a senior director and vice chairman of Sotheby's private sales worldwide for the Impressionist and Modern art department, "was aware of Bouvier's price manipulation and the essence of his scheme."<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/>

In November 2023, it was reported that Monaco investigating judges dismissed the case against Rybolovlev concerning his alleged complicity for invasion of privacy. A complaint against Rybolovlev as well as his lawyer Tetiana Bersheda and then-Monaco public prosecutor Jean-Pierre Dreno was filed back in 2015 by Tatia Rappo, a friend of both Rybolovlev and Bouvier. The case against Dreno was also dismissed in November 2023, whereas Bersheda was cleared of any wrongdoing by the Monaco court in March 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Esteve |first=Camille |date=2023-11-30 |title=Bouvier-Rybolovlev case: Jean-Pierre Dreno and Dmitry Rybolovlev cleared of invasion of privacy allegations |url=https://www.monaco-tribune.com/en/2023/11/bouvier-rybolovlev-case-jean-pierre-dreno-and-dmitry-rybolovlev-cleared-of-invasion-of-privacy-allegations/ |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Monaco Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2023, it was reported that Rybolovlev and Bouvier reached an undisclosed settlement agreement. According to a statement by the Geneva prosecutor's office, the parties requested that the criminal proceedings not be pursued.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinsella |first=Eileen |date=2023-12-11 |title=The Sprawling Legal Dispute Between Yves Bouvier and Dmitry Rybolovlev Is Finally Over |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/yves-bouvier-rybolovlev-dispute-settled-2406832 |access-date=2023-12-22 |website=Artnet News |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 8 January 2024, Rybolovlev's lawsuit against Sotheby's began in Manhattan federal court lasting nearly four weeks.  Rybolovlev personally testified in court through interpreters saying he fully relied on documents from Sotheby's when making art purchases through Bouvier, which eventually led him to overpay his art advisor up to $1 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fanelli |first=Kelly Crow and James |title=Sotheby's Cleared of Claims It Duped Russian Billionaire |url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/fine-art/sothebys-cleared-of-claims-it-duped-russian-billionaire-f419132f |access-date=2024-03-29 |work=WSJ |language=en-US}}</ref> Samuel Valette, Sotheby's senior vice president and head of private sales for EMEA, testified that the information in Bouvier's emails to Rybolovlev's aide to justify the price of artworks was “a complete fiction”.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinsella |first=Eileen |date=2024-01-19 |title=Sotheby's Exec Paints an Ugly Picture of Yves Bouvier's Deceptions in Ongoing Rybolovlev Trial |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/sothebys-exec-ugly-picture-rybolovlev-trial-2421077 |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Artnet News |language=en-US}}</ref>

On January 30, the ten-member jury found that the auction house didn't aid in defrauding Rybolovlev by secretly and significantly marking up the prices of 4 artworks sold to the Russian collector. Rybolovlev's lawyer said, however, that the case “achieved our goal of shining a light on the lack of transparency that plagues the art market,” adding, “That secrecy made it difficult to prove a complex aiding and abetting fraud case. This verdict only highlights the need for reforms, which must be made outside the courtroom.”<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-01-30 |title=Sotheby's Wins Suit by Russian Billionaire Over Art Fraud |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-01-30/sotheby-s-wins-suit-filed-by-russian-billionaire-over-art-fraud |access-date=2024-03-29 |work=Bloomberg.com |language=en}}</ref> 

On 6 June 2024, the ECHR issued a decision that confirmed the violation of Article 8 (right to respect for private life) of the European Convention on Human Rights of Rybolovlev’s lawyer, Tetiana Bersheda. The court ruled that during proceedings in Monaco, the judge “had extended the scope of his investigation too broadly and that the supervisory judicial authorities had failed to redefine the bounds of the expert’s assignment and of the investigation, in order to comply with the judge’s remit”. According to Rybolovlev’s attorney, Me Martin Reynaud, legal proceedings concerning corruption and influence peddling in Monaco could no longer continue as their basis was now considered illicitly obtained by Monegasque judiciary authorities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bregman |first=Alexandra |title='Monacogate' Feud Now Considered Human Rights Violation |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexandrabregman/2024/06/10/monacogate-feud-now-considered-human-rights-violation/ |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HUDOC - European Court of Human Rights |url=https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/#%7B%22itemid%22:%5B%22003-7965975-11107293%22%5D%7D |access-date=2024-06-20 |website=hudoc.echr.coe.int}}</ref>

In October 2024, Rybolovlev was cleared by Swiss authorities over his alleged role in the arrest of Yves Bouvier in Monaco in 2015. The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland initiated criminal proceedings in 2017 and accused Rybolovlev of “performing illegally for a foreign state” by allegedly arranging for Bouvier to be apprehended by Monaco’s police. After a thorough investigation, the Swiss attorney general’s office concluded that no suspicion justifying an indictment had been established and closed the case.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cassady |first=Daniel |date=2024-10-23 |title=Billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev Cleared in Swiss Investigation, Swiss Dealer Yves Bouvier Faces $830 M. Tax Bill |url=https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/rybolovlev-cleared-in-swiss-investigation-bouvier-faces-huge-tax-bill-1234721933/ |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=ARTnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In February 2025, the corruption and the influence-peddling case against Dmitry Rybolovlev was officially closed after Monaco’s judiciary ruled that the evidence presented was based on data unlawfully extracted from his lawyer's phone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boutry |first=Timothée |date=2025-02-27 |title=Soupçons de corruption : la justice monégasque enterre l’affaire Dmitri Rybolovlev |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/faits-divers/soupcons-de-corruption-la-justice-monegasque-enterre-laffaire-dmitri-rybolovlev-27-02-2025-DJMPUUTBMBHZ5AHKJ2VN5FJVKY.php |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=leparisien.fr |language=fr-FR}}</ref> The decision followed a ruling by the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), which stated that Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, concerning the right to privacy, had been violated. This effectively concluded the legal proceedings that had been ongoing since 2015. According to Rybolovlev's lawyers, there are no longer any criminal cases pending against him in any country in the world, and he is fully exonerated.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cassady |first=Daniel |date=2025-02-27 |title=Monaco Court Annuls Case Against Billionaire Art Collector Dmitry Rybolovlev |url=https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/monaco-court-annuls-case-dmitry-rybolovlev-yves-bouvier-1234733799/ |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=ARTnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2026, the documentary series ''The Oligarch and the Art Dealer'', directed by Andreas Dalsgaard and focusing on the long-running legal dispute between Dmitry Rybolovlev and Yves Bouvier, premiered at the [[Sundance Film Festival]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Program Guide {{!}} 2026 Sundance Film Festival |url=https://festival.sundance.org/program/film/6932f8bebd86511c1760f297 |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=festival.sundance.org}}</ref> The series was subsequently presented at [[CPH:DOX]] in Copenhagen (Denmark), the Visions du Réel festival in Nyon (Switzerland),<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Oligarch and the Art Dealer – Films |url=https://www.visionsdureel.ch/en/film/2026/the-oligarch-and-the-art-dealer/ |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Visions du Réel |language=en-US}}</ref> and in the Docuseries Competition section of [[2026 Canneseries|Canneseries]] in Cannes (France).<ref>{{Cite web |title=THE OLIGARCH AND THE ART DEALER |url=https://canneseries.com/en/series/the-oligarch-and-the-art-dealer |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Canneseries}}</ref> In June, the film was broadcast on the Arte television channel.

== Philanthropy ==
Rybolovlev provided financial assistance to the reconstruction of [[Saint Petersburg]]'s [[Oranienbaum Palace]], as well as to the restoration of the [[Conception Convent]] (also known as Zachatyevsky Monastery) in [[Moscow]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite news |date=5 June 2013 |title=Dmitry Rybolovlev: a Russian prince in Monaco |language=en |work=euronews |url=https://www.euronews.com/2013/06/05/dmitry-rybolovlev-a-russian-prince-in-monaco |access-date=19 October 2018 |archive-date=19 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019205645/https://www.euronews.com/2013/06/05/dmitry-rybolovlev-a-russian-prince-in-monaco |url-status=dead }}</ref> He donated €17.5 million for the re-building of the Cathedral of Nativity of Theotokos in Moscow, and was involved in the restoration of several icon paintings in the Cathedral of Exaltation of the Cross recreated in [[Belogorsky Monastery|Belogorsk Saint Nicolas Monastery]].<ref name=":9" /> He donated funds for the construction of the Russian Orthodox Church of [[Saint Nicholas|St Nicholas]] in [[Limassol, Cyprus]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Kathimerini |date=11 June 2012 |title=Οι ρωσόφωνοι αποκτούν τη "στέγη της πίστης" τους |trans-title=Russian Orthodox church in Cyprus |url=http://www.kathimerini.com.cy/index.php?pageaction=kat&modid=1&artid=93261&show=Y}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Is Dmitry Rybolovlev Football's Wise Man? |url=http://www.goldnews.com.cy/en/people/is-dmitry-rybolovlev-footballs-wise-man |access-date=19 October 2018 |website=goldnews.com.cy |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9" />

In 2010, Rybolovlev was awarded the Order of St [[Seraphim of Sarov]] I degree by [[Patriarch Kirill of Moscow|Patriarch Kirill]] for funding the restoration of the Cathedral of the Nativity of the Most Holy Mother of God in [[Zachatyevsky Convent]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Romfea |date=30 December 2010 |title=Ο Πατριάρχης Μόσχας τίμησε τον μεγιστάνα Dmitry Rybolovlev |url=http://www.romfea.gr/patriarxeia/patriarxeia/patriarxeio-mosxas/6996-6798}}</ref>

In April 2020, Rybolovlev donated the amount of 80 million rubles (more than $1 million) through his "Financial house" investment company to the Perm Territory Charitable Foundation to fight the [[COVID-19|coronavirus]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 April 2020 |title=Дмитрий Рыболовлев пожертвовал в краевой фонд по борьбе с коронавирусом 80 млн руб. |url=https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/4319882 |access-date=16 December 2021 |website=kommersant.ru |language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=ОВЧИННИКОВА |first=Алена |date=10 April 2020 |title=Дмитрий Рыболовлев пожертвовал Пермскому краю на борьбу с коронавирусом 80 миллионов рублей |url=https://www.perm.kp.ru/online/news/3831779/ |access-date=16 December 2021 |website=perm.kp.ru |language=ru}}</ref>

In October 2020, Rybolovlev announced he would donate €250,000 to help rebuild the pitch of [[Saint-Martin-Vésubie]], which was destroyed during [[Storm Alex]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 October 2020 |title=Le président de l'AS Monaco se mobilise pour reconstruire un stade à Saint-Martin-Vésubie |url=https://www.nicematin.com/faits-de-societe/le-president-de-las-monaco-se-mobilise-pour-reconstruire-un-stade-a-saint-martin-vesubie-587101 |access-date=10 December 2020 |website=Nice-Matin |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dmitri Rybolovlev va financer la reconstruction d'un stade à Saint-Martin-Vésubie |url=https://www.sofoot.com/dmitri-rybolovlev-va-financer-la-reconstruction-d-un-stade-a-saint-martin-vesubie-489805.html |access-date=10 December 2020 |website=SOFOOT.com |date=13 October 2020 |language=fr}}</ref> The donation follows a letter written by local 11-year-old twins to Rybolovlev asking for financial help for a stadium where ASM's academy spends a period of their pre-season every year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AS Monaco owner Rybolovlev offering €250k to rebuild Saint-Martin-Vésubie stadium after Storm Alex {{!}} Get French Football News |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2020/as-monaco-owner-rybolovlev-offering-e250k-to-rebuild-saint-martin-vesubie-stadium-after-storm-alex/ |access-date=16 December 2021 |website=www.getfootballnewsfrance.com|date=13 October 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=14 October 2020 |title=AS Monaco president announces personal donation to help rebuild football pitch destroyed by Storm Alex |url=https://www.monaco-tribune.com/en/2020/10/as-monaco-president-announces-personal-donation-to-help-rebuild-football-pitch-destroyed-by-storm-alex/ |access-date=10 December 2020 |website=Monaco Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

In November 2021, Rybolovlev's family charitable foundation was founded in Lefkada (Greece) to support his philanthropic activities in the region.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ΑΓΓΕΛΟΠΟΥΛΟΥ |first=ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΑ |date=11 November 2021 |title=Κοινωφελές ίδρυμα στην Ελλάδα από τον Ριμπολόβλεφ {{!}} ΕΛΛΑΔΑ |url=https://www.iefimerida.gr/ellada/koinofeles-idryma-stin-ellada-apo-ton-rimpoloblef |access-date=16 December 2021 |website=iefimerida.gr |language=el}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=ΔΕΛΕΒΕΓΚΟΣ |first=ΔΗΜΗΤΡΗΣ |title=Κοινωφελές ίδρυμα με αρχικό κεφάλαιο 150 χιλ. ευρώ δημιουργεί ο Ριμπολόβλεφ {{!}} Moneyreview.gr |url=https://www.moneyreview.gr/business-and-finance/business/55287/koinofeles-idryma-me-archiko-kefalaio-150-chil-eyro-dimioyrgei-o-rimpolovlef/ |access-date=16 December 2021 |website=www.moneyreview.gr}}</ref>

In 2022, in the wake of [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of Ukraine]], it was announced by AS Monaco that the club and Rybolovlev, in a personal capacity, donated to the Monegasque Red Cross to support its efforts of delivering humanitarian aid to civilian victims of the conflict.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Guerre en Ukraine : Dmitri Rybolovlev et l'AS Monaco annoncent des dons à la Croix-Rouge |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Guerre-en-ukraine-dmitri-rybolovlev-et-l-as-monaco-annoncent-des-dons-a-la-croix-rouge/1321110 |access-date=2022-03-10 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-09 |title=AS Monaco and its President Dmitry Rybolovlev support humanitarian aid |url=https://www.asmonaco.com/las-monaco-et-son-president-dmitry-rybolovlev-soutiennent-laide-humanitaire/ |access-date=2022-03-10 |website=AS Monaco |language=en-US}}</ref>

In April 2023, a new emergency department was opened at the [[Princess Grace Hospital Centre|Princess Grace Hospital Center]], fully funded by Rybolovlev for a total of 1.8 million euros.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inauguration du nouveau service des Urgences |url=https://www.chpg.mc/news-posts/inauguration-du-nouveau-service-des-urgences/ |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=CHPG |date=18 April 2023 |language=fr-FR}}</ref> The new building combines adult and pediatric emergency departments in one location with a dedicated technical platform and a versatile care team, while maintaining a pediatric specialization.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-04-20 |title=A Monaco, le service des urgences du CHPG remodelé pour plus d'efficacité |url=https://www.monacomatin.mc/sante/a-monaco-le-service-des-urgences-du-chpg-remodele-pour-plus-defficacite-842458 |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Monaco-Matin |language=fr}}</ref>

== Hobbies ==

Rybolovlev's hobbies include sailing where his yachts named '''Skorpis''' race competitively winning the [[ClubSwan 50 World Championship]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boatsnews.com/story/32138/clubswan-50-the-skorpios-crew-led-by-dmitri-rybolovlev-becomes-world-champion|title=ClubSwan 50, the Skorpios crew led by Dmitri Rybolovlev becomes world champion|date=17 October 2019 }}</ref> and taking line honour in the 2021 [[Fastnet Race]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sailweb.co.uk/2021/08/10/rolex-fastnet-race-skorpios-takes-line-honours-in-cherbourg/|title=Rolex Fastnet Race – Skorpios takes line honours in Cherbourg|author=James Boyd|date=2021-08-10}}</ref> sailing his [[ClubSwan 125]].

Dmitry Yevgenyevich Rybolovlev (Russian: Дмитрий Евгеньевич Рыболовлев, IPA: [ˈdmʲitrʲɪj jɪvˈɡʲenʲjɪvʲɪtɕ rɨbɐˈlovlʲɪf]; born 22 November 1966) is a Russian oligarch, billionaire businessman, and investor.
Rybolovlev became chairman of the Russian fertilizer producer Uralkali in 1995. In 2010, he sold his majority share of Uralkali to three Kremlin-linked oligarchs for $6.5 billion. As of 2021, Rybolovlev had a reported net worth of $6.7 billion, which ranked him 391st on Forbes's list of billionaires. 
In 2011, Rybolovlev became the majority owner and president of the football club Monaco. He is one of the alleged victims of Swiss art transporter Yves Bouvier as part of The Bouvier Affair.
His hobbies include sailing where his yachts named Skorpis race competitively, winning the ClubSwan 50 World Championship and taking line honour in the 2021 Fastnet Race sailing his ClubSwan 125.
